title: Video QA checks
summary: A collection of nouns and verbs for automated checks on an encoded video beyond the eight post-encode checks: blank and frozen frames, cut cadence, loudness range and true peak, clipping and silence gaps, caption timing against speech, caption line length and reading speed, safe areas, the file's delivery spec read from its own boxes, and a legibility proxy for rendered text, each measured on the exact bytes with tested standard-library code.
boundaries: Every check measures the exact bytes it names; a person decides what a finding means.
The code parses logs and boxes; it runs no FFmpeg, decodes nothing and calls no model.
A failed or not-run check stays on the record; the next attempt gets its own report.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs; an authorized requester enqueues the proposals worth doing.
Importing the pack writes nothing, enqueues nothing and installs no code.

nouns.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for automated checks on an encoded video beyond the eight post-encode checks

value.lets_workers: Run measured checks on the exact bytes of an encoded video that the video and motion pack's eight post-encode checks do not cover: blank and frozen frames against declared holds, cut cadence and stretches with almost no visual change, loudness range, true peak and the quietest window, silence gaps and clipping, caption sidecars linted for line length, reading speed, gaps and parity and timed against measured speech, the delivery spec read from the MP4's own boxes, and a legibility proxy for text whose size is known. Every check reports its measurement, limit and findings with times, and one report binds them to the file's SHA-256.

flow.when: The eight post-encode checks come first, preferably by a different worker.
Run the pinned FFmpeg analyses on the exact file and keep every log.
Lint the WebVTT and SRT sidecars and time them against speech.
Blank, frozen and cadence rows from the logs and the plan.
The MP4's boxes against the export spec.
Text sizes, reading time and safe areas for text whose size is known.
One report per file, with a verdict that follows from its rows.
A person or a different worker reviews the cut with the report.

value.worked_example: Made-up, recomputed by the code's tests: a 12-second vertical cut with a declared end-card hold, pause and fade. The report finds a fast first caption and a 67 ms blink gap, a short black flash and a white frame, a 1.7 s freeze, a 4 s stretch with almost no visual change, a quiet window and a silence outside the declared pause, a file whose moov box comes after its media data, and an AI-voice label under the platform's caption overlay. Its verdict is fail.
value.complements: The video and motion pack's check-video runs eight checks every cut must pass. This pack adds the checks a reviewer otherwise does by eye or by hand, with tested standard-library code, and leaves the judgment to the video review pack.
provenance_notes: Generalizes the automated gates of a working short-form video studio, which separates checks that block (frozen, silent, hookless, near-silent) from warnings a person weighs, and the every-frame, typography and audio checks of its audit question bank.
Shaped by ta-amps's own 3:00 explainer film on October 30, 2026, whose sidecar captions, loudness, freezes and MP4 boxes these checks were run on while this pack was written.

nouns.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.

value.how_it_is_checked: The extended QA report's media sha256 equals the digest of the delivered file, and every log in the measurement set names that digest.

nouns.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.

nouns.title: Guardrail: a check that did not run is never a pass
nouns.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.

nouns.title: Guardrail: passing checks is not approval
nouns.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.

value.rule: Automated checks find candidates; a person decides. A pass means no measured problem, not a good video: a meter cannot hear a muddy voice, and a size rule cannot see text over a busy picture. Only a person approves publishing.

nouns.title: Nine extended checks on an encoded video, with thresholds
nouns.category_reason: A suite of checks with thresholds and methods that every encoded file is measured against.

value.summary: Checks the eight post-encode checks leave to a person's eye or ear, each measured from the delivered bytes and reported with its limit. Thresholds are defaults from one production, not standards; a requester can override any of them and the report records which applied.

checks.threshold: No black run (blackdetect) or flat frame of any brightness (signalstats luma range of 16 or less) outside declared black; a run of 0.5 s or more fails, a shorter one warns.
No freeze (freezedetect, noise 0.001) outside declared holds plus a 0.75 s easing tail; 1.5 s warns, 2.0 s fails.
Cuts where the scene score reaches 0.12; any stretch of 4 s or more with a scene score under 0.002, outside holds, warns. Reports cuts per minute and the longest and median shot.

Integrated loudness within 1 LU of the target (-16 LUFS for web players, -14 for short social cuts) and true peak at or below -1 dBTP fail; a loudness range over 10 LU or a 3 s short-term window under -28 LUFS outside declared pauses warns.
Silence under -45 dB (silencedetect) outside declared pauses: 0.5 s warns, 2.0 s fails.
A sample peak at or above -0.1 dBFS with flat tops or 3 or more peak samples (astats) fails.

At most 2 lines of 42 characters, 1 to 7 s, at most 17 characters per second, no overlap, no 1 or 2 frame gap, cues in order and inside the media, WebVTT and SRT equal; at least 0.95 of speech covered, no cue without speech, cues starting no more than 0.5 s before or 0.3 s after their words (warn).

Every item of the export spec read from the MP4's boxes: fast start, fragments, codec, profile, chroma, size, frame rate and constancy, colour primaries, even dimensions, audio codec, object type, rate and channels, duration, size and bitrate budgets, and edit lists when the spec forbids them.

Text the viewer must read is at least its role's share of frame height (title 4.5%, caption 2.6%, body 2.2%, label 1.7%, fine print 1.2%) and at least 12 CSS px on the smallest planned display; it stays on screen for 0.5 s plus 3 words per second; boxes stay inside the safe area (warn) and clear of keep-out boxes (fail).

rules: Every row reports its measurement and limit, not only a result.
fail blocks the report's verdict; warn is recorded for a person to weigh; not_run carries its reason and makes the report incomplete.
A dissolve or a camera move rarely scores as a cut, so shot lengths are upper bounds and still stretches are warnings.
The legibility proxy runs only on text whose size is known from the stage, the layout or a measurement; it says nothing about weight, stroke, motion or a busy background.
The post-encode checks are defined once in the video and motion pack and are not repeated here.

Contrast follows the accessibility audit pack's contrast method: unrounded thresholds, large text from 24 px or 18.66 px bold. The page and player around a video, with its captions track, controls and audio description, are audited by that pack's check-media, not here.
A single frame with known layout, such as an end card or a cover, can also go through the screenshot design review pack, which uses the same 12 px text floor as its team default.

nouns.title: Measurement rules: the FFmpeg runs whose logs the checks read
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same file always gives the same logs and rows.

steps: Hash the file first; every log names that digest.
Picture: ffmpeg -nostats -i FILE -an -vf "blackdetect=d=0.1:pix_th=0.10,freezedetect=n=0.001:d=1.0" -f null - 2> picture.log
Luma range: ffmpeg -i FILE -an -vf "signalstats,metadata=mode=print:key=lavfi.signalstats.YMIN:file=ymin.txt,metadata=mode=print:key=lavfi.signalstats.YMAX:file=ymax.txt" -f null -
Scene scores, on a small copy for speed: ffmpeg -i FILE -an -vf "scale=480:-2,select='gte(scene,0)',metadata=mode=print:key=lavfi.scene_score:file=scenes.txt" -f null -
Loudness with true peak and the per-frame log, which FFmpeg writes only at the verbose level: ffmpeg -nostats -v verbose -i FILE -vn -af "ebur128=peak=true:framelog=verbose" -f null - 2> ebur128.log
Silence: ffmpeg -nostats -i FILE -vn -af "silencedetect=noise=-45dB:d=0.5" -f null - 2> silence.log
Clipping: ffmpeg -nostats -i FILE -vn -af "astats=measure_overall=Peak_level+Peak_count+RMS_level+Number_of_samples+Flat_factor:measure_perchannel=none" -f null - 2> astats.log
Keep every log as a noun with its digest, beside the QA plan it was measured against.
gotchas: The scdet filter prints only the frames it calls cuts; the per-frame scene score from select and metadata gives the whole series.
Some static FFmpeg builds have no drawtext filter; label contact sheets outside FFmpeg.
A freeze detector counts a black run as frozen too; read both rows together.
Logs carry FFmpeg's memory addresses, which differ between runs; compare parsed values, not log bytes.

Judge whether a video is good, true or ready; a person decides.
Write inside the seed-pack library; it refuses an output path there.

verbs.title: Collect the FFmpeg measurements of one file
verbs.summary: Hash the exact file, then run the pinned FFmpeg analyses on it and keep every log as a noun with its digest, beside the QA plan.
verbs.outcome: A measurement set: every log, its command and digest, for one file.

slots.name: encoded_output
slots.description: Pin of the encoded file's media noun.

slots.name: qa_plan
slots.description: Pin of the QA plan, declared before measuring.

network: Only the worker's own machine: FFmpeg reads a local copy of the file and writes local logs.
steps: Hash the file and confirm the digest matches the media noun.
Run each pinned FFmpeg analysis on that file and keep the logs unedited.
Write the measurement set with every command, log path and log digest, and the QA plan's pin.

acceptance.check: The output validates against template.measurement-set's schema.
The media sha256 equals the digest of the pinned media noun's file.
The QA plan's version predates every log in the set.

verbs.title: Lint the caption sidecars and time them against speech
verbs.summary: Parse the WebVTT and SRT sidecars, lint every cue for lines, length, reading speed, duration, gaps, overlaps and order, compare the two sidecars, and time each cue against measured speech intervals, listing problems without fixing them.
verbs.outcome: A captions row with every problem and the timing measurements.

slots.name: caption_track
slots.description: Pin of the caption track with its WebVTT and SRT sidecars.

slots.name: narration_track
slots.description: Pin of the narration track whose measured speech the cues are timed against.

max_cps.description: Most characters per second a cue may read at.

steps: Run the captions command of the pinned code on both sidecars, with speech intervals when a narration track is pinned.
List every problem with its cue and time; never edit the cues to make them pass.
Without speech intervals, report the sync part as not measured, with the reason.

acceptance.check: The output validates against template.check-rows's schema.
Running lint, parity and speech_sync on the pinned sidecars gives exactly the listed problems.
No new version of the caption track is written.

verbs.title: Check blank and frozen frames and the cut cadence
verbs.summary: From the measurement set and the QA plan, report black and flat frames, frozen stretches and the cut cadence, with every finding's times, honoring only the spans the plan declared.
verbs.outcome: Three rows: blank_frames, frozen_stretches and cut_cadence.
steps: Run the picture command of the pinned code on the logs and the plan.
Report each finding with its start and end; a missing log makes its row not_run with the reason.

acceptance.check: The output validates against template.check-rows's schema.
check_blank, check_frozen and check_cadence on the pinned logs give exactly these rows.
The QA plan pinned here is the version the measurement set names.

verbs.title: Check loudness, silence and clipping
verbs.summary: From the measurement set and the QA plan, report integrated loudness against the target, true peak, loudness range, the quietest short-term window, silence gaps outside declared pauses, and clipping.
verbs.outcome: Three rows: loudness, silence_gaps and clipping.

target_lufs.description: Integrated loudness target: -16 for web players, -14 for short social cuts.

steps: Run the sound command of the pinned code with the target the export spec names.
Say in the summary that a person still listens: the rows measure levels, not how the mix sounds.

acceptance.check: The output validates against template.check-rows's schema.
check_loudness, check_silence and check_clipping on the pinned logs give exactly these rows.
The loudness row's limit names the target that applied.

verbs.title: Check the file against its export spec
verbs.summary: Read the MP4's boxes with the pinned code and compare every item of the export spec, from fast start to the size budget, reporting what the file says and what it does not say.
verbs.outcome: A file_spec row with one item per spec entry.

slots.name: encoded_output
slots.description: Pin of the encoded file's media noun.

slots.name: export_spec
slots.description: Pin of the export spec from the video editing pack.

network: Only the worker's own machine: the code reads a local copy of the file.
steps: Run the filespec command on the file and the export spec's profile for this cut.

verbs.summary: For every piece of text whose size is known, compute its share of frame height and its CSS pixels on the smallest planned display, check its time on screen against its reading time, and check its box against the safe area and keep-out boxes.

Every item's size comes from the stage, the layout or a recorded measurement.
